Enabling switches on the node's own firmware-writing tool, and on a Compute Module 4 it also adds the chip settings that board needs. bootloaderSection.enableConfirmTitle: Allow EEPROM flashing from the OS?
bootloaderSection.enableCm4Message: This lets the platform flash a signed bootloader from the running system instead of via SD/USB. On a Compute Module 4 the node reboots immediately when you confirm.
bootloaderSection.enableCm4Hint: On a Compute Module 4 the change also writes SPI settings into config.txt, and those settings take effect only at boot, which is why the node reboots right away. It does not enable the distribution’s own automatic EEPROM updates.
bootloaderSection.enableUnknownMessage: This lets the platform flash a signed bootloader from the running system instead of via SD/USB. This board was not recognised, so whether it reboots cannot be determined in advance — on a Compute Module 4 it restarts immediately, elsewhere it does not. Treat it as though the node will reboot. It does not enable the distribution’s own automatic EEPROM updates.
bootloaderSection.enableNoRebootMessage: This lets the platform flash a signed bootloader from the running system instead of via SD/USB. It writes one configuration file and does not reboot the node. It does not enable the distribution’s own automatic EEPROM updates.
bootloaderSection.confirmUpdateMessage: Flash the latest signed bootloader (EEPROM firmware) on this node? The write itself does not reboot the node. The new bootloader takes effect on the next reboot, which this panel offers as a separate, confirmed step. The platform's boot order (network boot first, local storage as fallback) replaces whatever boot order the device arrived with. Do not power off the node while flashing runs: an interrupted write can leave the device unbootable until recovered over USB.
bootloaderSection.confirmUpdateMessageRecovery: Flash the latest signed bootloader (EEPROM firmware) on this node? The node is in recovery, so it reboots within seconds to apply the update, and an open terminal disconnects. The platform's boot order (network boot first, local storage as fallback) replaces whatever boot order the device arrived with. Do not power off the node while flashing runs: an interrupted write can leave the device unbootable until recovered over USB.

usb.description: Flash a CM4/CM5 EEPROM over USB. Put the device into usbboot (nRPI_BOOT) mode, connect it, then Connect below — the board serial is read automatically. The EEPROM is written with a node token, so the board boots from the network first and adopts itself into this account.

usb.leaseDays_other: Power the device on within {{count}} days of flashing.

ssh.intro: Adopt a device that is already running an OS. Test the connection, then adopt: the platform installs the agent, registers the node and (if enabled) flashes a network-first EEPROM. Installing the agent and flashing reboot the device.
ssh.hostKeyChanged: The device's SSH host key changed since the connection test, so no credentials were sent. Was {{expected}}, now {{observed}}. If the device was reinstalled, accept the new key. Otherwise, check that this is the device you expect.
ssh.hostKeyFirstContact: First time this key was seen.
ssh.hostKeyFirstContactHint: The platform stores no host keys. Later tests and the adoption check that the device still presents this key. A reinstalled device presents a new key, and you will be asked to accept it. Trust lasts while this panel is open and the host stays the same.
ssh.hostKeyVerified: Matches the key from the earlier test.
ssh.hostKeyStillTrusted: Still expecting host key {{fingerprint}} from the earlier test.
ssh.unsupportedArchitecture: Unsupported architecture: {{arch}} — the agent package is arm64.
ssh.sudoPasswordNeeded: This device needs a sudo password to install the agent — fill the "Sudo password" field and try again.
ssh.sudoPasswordRejected: The sudo password was rejected by the device — check it and try again.
ssh.agentNote: Authenticates using your forwarded ssh-agent — the device must already trust your key (e.g. a YubiKey). Add the agent socket forward to your tunnel (no server-side script needed):
ssh.agentTouchNote: Touch the YubiKey if it prompts during connect/adopt. Requires ssh_adopt.allow_agent_auth on the server (an on-prem / single-team feature — connection keys are the multi-user path).
ssh.noConnectionKeys: No connection keys yet — generate one on the SSH Keys tab, then install its public part on the device.
ssh.reAdoptingSuffix: — its existing name and credentials are kept, so no new-node details are needed.
ssh.networkFirstCheckbox: Flash a network-first boot order into the EEPROM after the agent connects.
ssh.adoptWarning: Adoption installs the agent and, if enabled, reflashes the EEPROM. The device will reboot, and a reflash overwrites its boot configuration. Make sure this is the right device.
ssh.ackReboot: I understand the device will reboot.
ssh.alreadyRegisteredIntro: This device is already registered as
ssh.alreadyRegisteredSuffix: . Adopting will re-use that node — it won't create a duplicate.

single.intro: Create the node record, then download its one-time SD boot image from the node's details panel. The device binds to this node on first boot and comes up already approved.

single.networkFirstCheckbox: Network-first — flash the EEPROM to netboot on first boot (the device reboots once during onboarding).
